# Error codes

<!-- Generated by scripts/Update-AutomatedPackagingErrorCodes.ps1 from docs/reference/error-codes.md
     of the product repository, commit 04e6d91. Do not edit this page by hand. -->

This page lists every `AP-` error code of AppVentiX Automated Packaging, with its cause and what to do. The product generates this list from its own code. [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#common-error-codes) has the short list of common codes.

A code never gets a different meaning. A code that is no longer used stays in the list, marked retired.

*Copied from the product's error-code register of 2026-11-02 (commit 04e6d91).*

## `AP-HV` — VM lifecycle

### `AP-HV-006` — The worker VM stopped unexpectedly

The VM left the running state while a job was in progress, and the host did not ask it to; or it stopped responding and its heartbeat did not come back; or it restarted after a stop error or a reset, which the guest's System log records. This is the guest crashing rather than the installer rebooting it, which is AP-IN-009.

**What to do:**

- Read the job's failure detail: it says whether the VM stopped, went silent, or restarted uncleanly. For a stop, check the Hyper-V-Worker event log on the host for the reason. The worker itself is reverted after the job, so its own logs of the crash are gone.
- Confirm the host has enough free memory to keep an 8 GB guest resident.
- Revert the worker to its baseline checkpoint and run the job again.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-HV-007` — The worker is already running a job

The worker this job needs holds a live lease for another job, so it was not touched. A worker runs one package at a time. Other workers can run other jobs at the same time.

**What to do:**

- Wait for the other job to finish, or cancel it from the Jobs screen.
- Let the planner choose the machine: it uses another free worker for the same target.
- If no job is running, a process that stopped still holds the lease. Open the window: the Jobs screen offers to recover it.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-HV-008` — The worker could not be created

Creating the virtual machine was refused before anything was built: a machine of that name already exists, its disk is already there, or the host has no room for it. Nothing was changed, so a machine that already holds work is left exactly as it was.

**What to do:**

- Choose a different worker name, or remove the existing machine yourself. The product never deletes a virtual machine.
- Check free space where the workers live. One worker needs at least 60 GB free, and 200 GB is recommended for several.
- Confirm the name begins with the managed prefix, which is the only name the product will act on.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-HV-009` — The virtual TPM could not be enabled

Windows 11 Setup will not install without a TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot, and the key protector that a virtual TPM needs could not be created. Caught here rather than left alone, because otherwise it surfaces much later as Setup refusing the machine for reasons it does not explain.

**What to do:**

- On a managed host, check whether Host Guardian Service configuration blocks Set-VMKeyProtector.
- Confirm the host supports virtualisation-based security and that the worker is Generation 2.
- Build the worker on a host that can give it a virtual TPM.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-HV-010` — The worker could not be removed

Removing the virtual machine was refused and nothing was deleted. It is running, it is not there at all, or the hypervisor would not remove it. Refusing is the safe outcome here: this is the one operation in the product that cannot be undone.

**What to do:**

- Stop the machine first. A running worker is one something is using, and removal never pulls its power.
- Check whether the machine is already gone. Being asked to remove something twice reads as a failure rather than as a success, deliberately.
- Confirm the name begins with the managed prefix, which is the only name the product will act on.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-HV-011` — The worker could not be put back to its baseline

Restoring the baseline checkpoint failed, so the machine is in whatever state the last thing to touch it left. Nothing else is offered it until somebody says so: a worker whose state nobody knows is how one job's leftovers end up inside the next job's package.

**What to do:**

- Check that the baseline checkpoint still exists on the machine. An update re-seals it, and a re-seal interrupted half way can leave none.
- Check free space where the workers live. Applying a checkpoint writes before it discards.
- Confirm nothing else has the machine open in Hyper-V Manager with a dialog waiting.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-HV-012` — AI agents do not remove workers on this host

An AI agent asked through MCP to remove a worker or to forget an image. On this host, agents do not do this. Removing a worker deletes the machine and its disks.

**What to do:**

- Remove the worker or forget the image on the Images screen, or with the command line.
- To let agents do it, go to Settings > AI agents (MCP). Select "Agents can remove workers and forget images", then click Save.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-NW` — Channel and network

### `AP-NW-004` — The worker's clock could not be corrected

The guest clock was set, re-measured, and is still outside tolerance. When the remaining skew equals the age of the checkpoint and never converges, Time Synchronization is disabled on the VM.

**Observed:** Skew equal to the checkpoint age, never converging across repeated corrections.

**What to do:**

- Enable the Time Synchronization integration service on the worker VM.
- Confirm the host clock is itself correct.
- Re-take the baseline checkpoint once the guest clock is right.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-NW-005` — The connection to the agent was lost

The guest heartbeat is present and the agent process is alive, but the gRPC channel dropped and reconnection did not succeed. This is a transport fault rather than a guest failure.

**What to do:**

- Check whether the network mode changed mid-job, which tears down the channel.
- Confirm the vSwitch port ACLs still permit the agent to reach the host on its listener port.
- Check the host firewall for a rule blocking the listener.

**Retry:** Yes. This is a transient condition.

### `AP-NW-006` — The DNS sinkhole is not working

A name resolved slower than one second, or did not resolve at all, during the startup self test. Left undetected this appears much later as an unexplained 12 second hang in the middle of a conversion.

**Observed:** A host with nine enabled inbound Allow rules covering UDP, none of which applied to the responder, so the guest's query was dropped before the sinkhole saw it.

**What to do:**

- Run host preparation, which creates the inbound firewall rule the responder needs.
- Check for Windows PowerShell 'Query User' inbound Block rules, which Windows recreates and which defeat the sinkhole silently.
- Confirm the responder is bound to the host vNIC address rather than a wildcard listener only.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-NW-007` — The worker sent more than this host accepts

An upload was refused because it exceeded the host's own ceiling, per file or for the whole job. The size an agent declares is a claim, not a limit: a guest is untrusted once an installer has run in it, so the host keeps its own bound and enforces it as the bytes arrive.

**What to do:**

- Check whether the package really is this large; a capture that swept in a whole profile can be.
- Raise MaxJobUploadMegabytes in agent-channel.json if it genuinely is. One artifact may be half of it.
- If the size is unexpected, review the image's exclusion set before raising the limit.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-AG` — Agent and bootstrapper

### `AP-AG-002` — The image's bootstrapper is too old for this agent

The bootstrapper in the golden image declares a contract major version the agent does not accept. The bootstrapper is deliberately thin so this should be rare, and when it happens the image needs rebaking.

**What to do:**

- Rebuild the golden image with the current bootstrapper.
- Until then, use an image whose bootstrapper matches.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-AG-003` — The agent binary is not correctly signed

Authenticode verification of the agent failed. An unsigned or tampered agent is never run in a VM that produces signed customer artifacts, so this blocks unconditionally.

**What to do:**

- Reinstall the product to restore an intact agent binary.
- If this persists, the installation may have been modified on disk. Verify the install directory.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-AG-005` — The agent stopped running inside the worker

The guest heartbeat is still present but the agent process is gone. The VM is healthy; the agent is not.

**What to do:**

- Collect the agent log from the worker before reverting, since the revert discards it.
- Check the guest Application event log for a crash record.
- Run the job again; if it reproduces at the same stage, capture a diagnostics bundle.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-AG-006` — The agent in the image could not be updated

The host offered a newer agent than the image carries and the update did not complete, so the worker is still running the old one. A stale agent is reported rather than used quietly, because a version mismatch produces failures that get attributed to the wrong layer.

**What to do:**

- Check the worker can still reach the host on the listener port: the agent fetches its replacement over the same channel it reports on.
- Confirm the offered agent is signed and that its certificate is trusted inside the image.
- Rebuild the image with a current agent if the update keeps failing.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-AG-007` — This worker's image does not record an agent identity

Each worker enrols for its own client certificate during preparation, and the image record keeps its thumbprint. A job token is bound to that thumbprint, so a worker whose image names none cannot be given a token at all. An image built before enrolment recorded one is the usual cause.

**What to do:**

- Run Update on this worker: step 6 re-enrols it and rewrites the image record in place.
- If the update cannot run, rebuild the image from media.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-AG-008` — The worker refused its guest account's password

The host signs in to the worker with the password it stored when the worker was built, and the worker refused it. Windows also refuses the worker's own automatic sign-in then, so the agent never starts. A worker built before 0.2.14 has a password that expires 42 days after it was built; that is the usual cause.

**Observed:** The guest's own log refuses the automatic sign-in with 0xC0000071 (password expired), and PowerShell Direct answers "The credential is invalid".

**What to do:**

- Rebuild the worker from media on the Images screen. A worker built from 0.2.14 on keeps its password.
- If the worker was built from 0.2.14 on, its stored password and the guest no longer agree: rebuild it.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-IM` — Worker image

### `AP-IM-008` — The image's exclusion set is incomplete

The exclusion set does not restate the entries MPT excludes by default. MPT does not merge its built-in list with a supplied one, it replaces it, so anything not restated is captured.

**Observed:** MPT's own logs and MsixGenerator.ConversionState.xml landing inside the package, roughly doubling its size.

**What to do:**

- Recalibrate the image, which regenerates the exclusion set including the floor.
- Compare the set against the shipped baseline; a set smaller than the floor is always wrong.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-009` — The packaging tool's licence is not registered in the image

MPT is present but its offline licence was never registered for the account that runs conversions. The licence step needs a second, undocumented registration call beyond installing the package.

**Observed:** MPT vanishing after a reboot, or conversions failing 0x80072EE7 or 'the file cannot be accessed by the system'.

**What to do:**

- Re-run the image's MPT licence step, including the -Register call.
- Confirm the registration ran as the same account the agent uses.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-010` — The packaging driver is missing from the image

MPT's filter driver is not installed, or its build does not match the guest OS release family. Capture cannot run without it.

**Observed:** 0x8024402C during driver fetch, or 0x800f081f CBS_E_SOURCE_MISSING.

**What to do:**

- Install the driver from Features on Demand media matching the guest's release family.
- If FoD media is unavailable, give the image a one-time internet window and let MPT fetch the driver.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-011` — Image preparation ran in the wrong order

Hardening disabled Windows Update before the packaging driver was installed. The ordering is absolute: the driver has to be in place first, because installing it needs the update stack.

**Observed:** Add-WindowsCapability failing 0x80240438 because Windows Update is disabled.

**What to do:**

- Rebuild the image, installing the MPT driver before applying any hardening.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-012` — The worker does not have enough free disk space

A capture needs room for the installed application, MPT's own working files and the package being built, all at once. The minimum is an Advanced setting and defaults to 10 GB.

**What to do:**

- Lower the minimum in Advanced if this application is small and the default is too conservative.
- Give the worker a larger disk, or revert it to a baseline taken before it accumulated state.
- A real conversion of a 283 MB installer unpacked to 2.7 GB of VFS, so the requirement is not proportional to the installer's size.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-013` — The installation media is missing or does not match the guest

A file the build needs was not where it was configured to be, or the Features on Demand media belongs to a different Windows release family than the guest. A mismatched family does not satisfy the capture driver, and the product ships no Microsoft binaries, so all of this is supplied rather than fetched.

**What to do:**

- Check the configured media paths.
- Match the Features on Demand media to the guest release family: 22621 media serves Windows 11 22H2, 26100 serves 24H2 and later.
- Confirm the packaging tool package and its licence are both present. The licence is a separate file and is the one most often missed.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-014` — Windows did not finish installing

The unattended install did not reach a logged-on desktop within the time allowed. An answer file that Setup rejects leaves the machine on a prompt nobody is watching, which is indistinguishable from a slow install until the time runs out.

**What to do:**

- Open the worker's console and read what Setup is waiting for.
- Confirm the answer file is attached as a DVD drive, and that the edition it names is one the installation media actually carries.
- Check the host still has room. An install that fills the volume stops rather than failing.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IM-015` — Tamper Protection is on, so hardening would not hold

Tamper Protection cannot be switched off from a running Windows by anything, including SYSTEM, because enforcement sits below the ACL layer in a protected process. Settings applied while it is on revert a few seconds later with no error, and Defender activity then lands in every capture with no visible cause.

**What to do:**

- Turn Tamper Protection off in Windows Security, then run this again. It cannot be disabled from PowerShell, WMI or the registry by design.
- Better: shut the worker down and run scripts\image\Disable-WorkerDefender.ps1 -WorkerName <name>. It disables the six Defender services in the offline SYSTEM hive, so Defender never starts and has nothing to protect. This is the route that works on every build; the answer file's writes during specialize are reverted on the build the product installs.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-016` — The runtimes could not be installed in an isolated guest

The redistributables the packaging tool depends on were not staged locally, and an isolated guest has no route to a package source. Reaching for the network instead would open a guest that is isolated by design.

**What to do:**

- Stage the redistributables on the host and point the image preparation at them.
- The set is the Visual C++ runtimes, the .NET Desktop Runtime and the WebView2 runtime.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-017` — Calibration did not produce a usable exclusion set

Too few null captures completed, or their union was empty. Variance between runs of one image is larger than the difference between Windows builds, so a single empty result means nothing and must not be adopted: four identical captures from one checkpoint measured 534, 0, 534 and 534 registry keys.

**What to do:**

- Run at least four null captures, one of them a long window of about three minutes, and take the union of the results.
- Reboot and let the image settle first. Calibrating straight after a hardening change measures the change's own aftershock rather than the image's resting state.
- Confirm the capture driver is installed and the packaging tool starts. A capture that never ran produces an empty delta that looks like a quiet image.

**Retry:** Yes. This is a transient condition.

### `AP-IM-018` — The image's calibration has expired

The exclusion set was measured long enough ago that Windows has had time to change what an idle guest writes. The consequence is not a job that fails: it is a package quietly carrying somebody else's noise, which is why this is raised rather than left to a warning.

**What to do:**

- Re-calibrate the image, then take a new baseline checkpoint.
- If the image is no longer maintained, forget it so that no job can select it.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-019` — A script the product ships is not signed like the product

A signed product runs only the scripts signed the way it is itself, and this one was not: it is unsigned, changed since it was signed, or signed by somebody else. These scripts run elevated on this host or inside a worker, so the step stopped before running or copying it. An unsigned product checks nothing.

**What to do:**

- Repair or reinstall the product: the installer puts back the scripts it signed.
- If a script was changed on purpose, it has to be signed with the product's certificate again; a changed script is never run.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-020` — A preparation step stopped on an error it has no code for

A step that builds or updates a worker ran a Windows or Hyper-V operation, and it failed with an error this product does not classify. The message is the operation's own, and the step it happened in is named.

**What to do:**

- Read the preparation's log, prep-<worker>-<run>.log in the Logs folder of the working directory: its last lines name the step and give the whole error.
- The machine is left as the step found it. A worker being built that did not reach step 12 is listed under Incomplete machines; an Update's worker stays on the Images screen, where Put it back or Rebuild from media start again once the cause is fixed.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IM-021` — Windows could not be activated against the KMS server

Step 9 opened the host's KMS relay, pointed the worker's Windows at it and asked it to activate, and Windows refused or could not reach the server. The message names the server that was tried and the code Windows answered with. The worker stays on the internal switch throughout: only the host talks to the KMS server, for at most three minutes.

**What to do:**

- Check the KMS server named in the message from this host: the host resolves the name and makes the connection, so a name only the workers' network knows does not resolve here.
- 0xC004F074 means no KMS server answered: the name, the port, a firewall between this host and the server, or the inbound rule for TCP 1688 that Prepare this host creates under Settings > This host.
- 0xC004F038 means the server answered and has not yet counted enough clients to activate any; 0xC004F042 means it will not activate this edition. Both are the KMS server's to fix.
- Build the image again, or Update it once the server is right: an Update may change the KMS server.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IM-022` — A prerequisite could not be installed on the image

Step 7 installs the prerequisites chosen for the image, in order, before hardening. One of them exited with a code that is not one of its success codes, asked for a restart it is not allowed, was not found by its detection rule afterwards, or did not finish in its time. The message names the item, its ID and what it answered.

**What to do:**

- Open the item on the Prerequisites screen and check its arguments, success codes and detection rule. An installer run without its silent switch waits for a click nobody can give.
- An item that needs a restart must have Restart allowed ticked; 3010 and 1641 are the codes that ask for one.
- Items must install offline: a web installer or a bootstrapper that downloads its payload fails on a worker, which has no route out.
- Build or Update the image again once the item is right. The worker is left as the step found it.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-IN` — Installer and capture

### `AP-IN-007` — Reboot budget exceeded (retired)

**RETIRED. Never raised.** Section 7 withdrew reboot support, so the budget this counted is unreachable. Recorded rather than deleted because codes are never reused.

### `AP-IN-008` — The job ran out of time

The whole job exceeded its limit. This is deliberately distinct from AP-IN-010, which is one MPT invocation overrunning: they point at different problems.

**What to do:**

- Check which stage was running when the limit hit; a large installer may simply need a longer limit.
- If the job was idle rather than busy, look for an installer waiting on a dialog nobody can answer.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IN-009` — The worker restarted during the capture

Something restarted the worker in the middle of the capture. The packaging tool cannot finish a capture across a restart: it resumes and then crashes building the package, or cannot resume at all (measured). An installer that only asks for a restart, with exit code 3010 or 1641, is handled without one; this is an installer, or a program it started, that restarted Windows by itself.

**Observed:** NullReferenceException in TranslateShortcutsToApplicationNode, an empty output directory, and HKLM\Software\Microsoft\MSIXPackagingTool\Resume still present.

**What to do:**

- Look for a vendor switch that suppresses the restart, such as /norestart, REBOOT=ReallySuppress for an MSI, or a documented no-reboot option. The work it left for the restart then runs inside the capture.
- If the installer restarts Windows whatever it is told, it cannot be captured. Package the application from an already-installed reference machine instead.
- Do not simply retry: it reproduces exactly.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-010` — The packaging tool stopped responding

One MPT invocation exceeded its hard timeout and the process tree was killed. MPT can stop on an internal error and wait on a keypress that nothing will ever send, so the product cannot rely on it exiting.

**Observed:** 'Press any key to close this window...' printed, the process alive at near-zero CPU, still running when checked ten minutes later. One conversion sat for 50 minutes against a 40 minute timeout.

**What to do:**

- Check the MPT log for 'Press any key to close this window', which is the wait-on-keypress case.
- If the log ends with 'Installer still running', the installer or a program it started never exited: the packaging tool waits for all of them. An installer that starts its application when it finishes is the usual cause; switch that off in its arguments (for VS Code, /MERGETASKS=!runcode).
- If the installer was alive at near-zero CPU with no output, its silent arguments are probably wrong and it reached a UI on a desktop nobody is looking at. Confirm the silent switches first.
- Retry only after understanding which of the two it was.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IN-011` — This installer needs silent-install arguments

An .exe installer was submitted with no Arguments and without the explicit UnattendedInstallWithoutArgument opt-out. MPT refuses the template outright, and it does so only after a VM has already started, so the product catches it at template generation instead.

**Observed:** MPT refusing to read the template and exiting 1, after a VM had already been started.

**What to do:**

- Supply the installer's silent switches. Vendor documentation is the first place to look, though it is not always right: one documented --silent switch reached a UI anyway, and /quiet /norestart worked.
- If the installer genuinely takes no arguments, set UnattendedInstallWithoutArgument deliberately.
- If it has no silent mode at all, use interactive install mode.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-012` — The installer did not report success

The installer ran and exited with a code that is not in this job's accepted list. Far and away the commonest cause is that the silent-install arguments are wrong: the installer started, could not do what it was told, and gave up.

**Observed:** A non-zero installer exit reported by MPT, with the capture completing anyway and producing a package containing little or nothing.

**What to do:**

- Check the silent switches against the vendor's documentation, and then against reality. One application's own documented --silent switch reached a UI anyway, on a desktop nobody was looking at; /quiet /norestart worked.
- 1603 is the generic MSI failure and usually means a prerequisite is missing or the arguments are malformed. 1618 means another install is in progress.
- If the code is legitimate for this installer, add it to the accepted list in Advanced. 3010 and 1641 cannot be added and need not be: they ask for a restart, and the install wrapper handles that itself by running the restart's work inside the capture.
- Check whether anything was actually installed. An empty capture delta with a non-zero exit means the installer did nothing at all.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-013` — The installer left work that only a restart can do

The installer finished, and scheduled work that Windows does only while restarting: files to be replaced or deleted at the next boot, or RunOnceEx work. The capture cannot run that work, so the package would hold the files as they were before the restart. The message and the install log name each entry. A file deleted at the restart in a folder the package leaves out, such as the temporary folder, does not cause this: it is noted on the job instead.

**What to do:**

- A file replaced at the restart usually means the installer found it in use. On a clean worker that is rare; look for a service or process the installer starts and then updates, and whether a vendor switch avoids it.
- Look for a variant of the installer that completes without a restart, such as a newer version, an MSI instead of a bundle, or a documented option that installs everything in one pass.
- Do not simply retry: it reproduces exactly.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-014` — A prerequisite could not be installed before the capture

The job installs its prerequisites on the reverted worker, in order, before it captures the application. One of them exited with a code that is not one of its success codes, asked for a restart it is not allowed, was not found by its detection rule afterwards, or did not finish in its time. Nothing was captured. The message names the item, its ID and what it answered.

**What to do:**

- Open the item on the Prerequisites screen and check its arguments, success codes and detection rule. An installer run without its silent switch waits for a click nobody can give.
- An item that needs a restart must have Restart allowed ticked; 3010 and 1641 are the codes that ask for one.
- Items must install offline: a web installer or a bootstrapper that downloads its payload fails on a worker.
- A PowerShell 7 script item needs the PowerShell 7 item it depends on; it is installed first when it is not on the image.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-015` — The files beside the installer could not be staged

The job was asked to take the files and folders beside the installer, or an MSI's transforms, to the worker with it, and could not: the folder had become a drive root, held a link or grew past the limit since the job was planned, a file changed size or now led somewhere else while it was being sent, a transform was gone or was a link, or the worker could not unpack them. Nothing was captured.

**What to do:**

- Keep the installer in a folder of its own with only the files it needs, and leave that folder alone while the job runs.
- The limit is 4 GB and 20,000 files beside the installer. Links (junctions, symbolic links) and files with a second name (hard links) are refused, because they can point anywhere on the host: replace them with copies.
- Check each transform still exists where it was chosen, as a file and not a link.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-016` — The installer changed after the job was planned, so it was not run

The job recorded the installer's SHA-256 when it was planned. When it sent the installer to the worker, the file was different, was gone, was a link, had a second name, or led to another folder. The worker did not run it, and nothing was captured.

**What to do:**

- Leave the installer and its folder alone while the job runs, then build the job again.
- Keep installers where only the people who package can change them. A share that others can write is a risk.
- Links (junctions, symbolic links) and files with a second name (hard links) are refused: replace them with a copy.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-AN` — Pre-analysis

### `AP-AN-010` — This MSI schedules a reboot

Pre-analysis found a ScheduleReboot or ForceReboot action in the installer's action table. This is a note, not a refusal: the MSI runs with /norestart, and the install wrapper runs the work it leaves in RunOnce inside the capture. Files it schedules for replacement at the restart refuse the package afterwards (AP-IN-013).

**Observed:** A ScheduleReboot or ForceReboot action present in the MSI action table.

**What to do:**

- Nothing to do before the build. If the job ends in AP-IN-013, look for a vendor switch or transform that avoids the restart.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-AN-011` — This installer declares a Windows service

The MSI declares services in its ServiceInstall table. These are captured and do work, but the resulting package carries the restricted capabilities packagedServices and localSystemServices. Informational, not a refusal.

**Observed:** An MSI-declared service packaged, deployed, running from inside the package, and removed cleanly on uninstall.

**What to do:**

- No action needed. Be aware the package requires restricted capabilities, which affects Store submission and some deployment policies.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-AN-012` — This file could not be read as an installer

The Build screen fills in the application name, publisher and version from the installer itself. This file either is not the type its extension claims, or its metadata is not readable. The job can still be described by hand; nothing is inferred from a file that will not open.

**What to do:**

- Check the download completed. A truncated MSI has the right extension and an unreadable database.
- If the file is an EXE with an installer inside it, there is nothing to pre-fill from. Enter the name, publisher and version, and supply the silent switches.
- If it is a genuine MSI that other tools open, keep the file: this is worth a support ticket with the code, because it means the database opened somewhere and not here.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-AN-013` — This installer installs a driver

Pre-analysis found a device or kernel driver in the MSI, so the job is refused before a VM is started. An MSIX package cannot install a driver: the capture would either leave it out or carry a driver file that nothing will ever load.

**What to do:**

- Deploy the driver separately — from the vendor's installer, Intune or Configuration Manager — and package the application without it, if the vendor offers a driver-free install.
- If the driver serves optional hardware, look for a vendor property that skips the driver feature and pass it in the silent arguments.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-PK` — Packaging

### `AP-PK-004` — The package contains part of the packaging tool

The post-capture scan found the agent install root or the product marker in the payload or the virtual registry. Shipping that to a customer's estate is not acceptable, so the job fails.

**What to do:**

- Check the image's always-on exclusions cover the agent install root.
- Confirm a null capture on this image comes back empty; a contaminated null capture means the image, not the application.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-005` — The package has nothing to launch

The produced manifest has an empty or missing Applications element. The package will install and do nothing, because the installer created no Start Menu shortcut for MPT to translate into an entry point.

**Observed:** Exit code 0, a package that installs cleanly, and nothing launchable. MPT logged only 'A shortcut with target ... was not detected'.

**What to do:**

- Check whether the installer creates a shortcut at all; many per-machine tools do not.
- If the application is genuinely shortcut-less, add one in the installer or supply the entry point manually before packaging.
- MPT logs this only as an informational line about a shortcut not being detected, so it is not a mistake you will find in its output.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-006` — The package declares a framework it does not use

MPT writes a Windows App SDK dependency into the manifest of every package that has an entry point, regardless of what the payload actually contains. Left in place the package will not deploy.

**Observed:** Add-AppxPackage failing 0x80073CF3, 'depends on a framework that could not be found', naming Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime.1.4 on a plain runFullTrust payload. MPT emits that same hard-coded version for every package, measured across six.

**What to do:**

- The product strips this automatically. Seeing this code means the payload scan was inconclusive rather than clearly negative.
- If the application genuinely is a Windows App SDK application, confirm the target machines carry a matching runtime version.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-007` — Something that should have been excluded is in the package

Post-conversion verification found a path the exclusion set was supposed to remove. Exclusion syntax fails silently: a wrong path form excludes nothing and MPT reports nothing, so the list cannot be trusted without checking the result.

**Observed:** Three excluded entries surviving into a package, including a 7.8 MB copy of the source MSI.

**What to do:**

- Check the path form of the offending exclusion against the documented syntax rules.
- An entry reported UNVERIFIABLE rather than failed means no mapping exists for it. That is not a pass and needs a person to look at it.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-008` — Some services were not carried into the package

Services appear in the capture but the manifest has no matching windows.service extension for them. These are services the installer created at run time rather than declaring, and MPT drops them silently. Reported rather than refused, because the commonest case by far is an auto-updater nobody wants packaged.

**Observed:** Run-time-created services present in the capture and absent from the manifest, with no warning from MPT.

**What to do:**

- Check the reported service names. An updater service is usually safe and often desirable to lose.
- If the application depends on one of them, it will not work from the package and needs a different packaging approach.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-PK-009` — The package contains a RunOnce entry that will never run

The installer registered work to be done after a restart. Windows reads RunOnce from the real registry, never from a package's virtual one, so that work silently never happens and the package looks fine.

**Observed:** HKLM\...\CurrentVersion\RunOnce present in a package's virtual registry after a conversion that otherwise succeeded.

**What to do:**

- Check what the entry does. Registering a file cleanup or a one-time migration is usually harmless to lose; finishing the installation is not.
- If the application depends on it, this installer needs its post-restart phase completing before capture, or it cannot be packaged this way.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-PK-010` — The package was built and its export did not complete

The job succeeded and the package is in the output folder, but copying it to the export location set on Settings did not complete. The warning says which step failed. When it is the package itself, whatever reads that location will not see this build. When the package was exported and only the self-signed certificate or the dependency list beside it was not written, the package is there without it.

**What to do:**

- Check that the export location on Settings is reachable from this host and that the account the application runs as can write to it. Check location on Settings tries exactly that.
- On a share (\\server\share), "access denied" is usually the share's own permissions, not the folder's: their default is Everyone: Read, which refuses every write through the share path even to an administrator and to this application running elevated. Give the account Change on the share, or, for a share on this host, use the folder's local path as the export location.
- A package folder or the Certificates folder under the export location that is a junction or a symbolic link is refused rather than written through. Remove the link; the export creates the folder itself.
- Copy the package from the output folder by hand, or build the job again once the location works.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-PK-011` — The Package Support Framework could not be applied

The job turns the Package Support Framework on, and its binaries on this host are missing, have changed since they were acquired, or are not signed by TMurgent Technologies LLP, who publish the release the product uses. The message names the files. Nothing was put into the package.

**What to do:**

- On Settings > This host, card Package Support Framework, press Get PSF (or Get … again). It downloads the pinned release from GitHub and checks every file before keeping it.
- On a host with no internet, put the files of that release into the PSF folder the card names, by hand.
- If the job does not need PSF, turn it off in the job's Advanced settings.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-012` — A prerequisite cannot be used

An image or a job asks for a prerequisite whose files in the working directory's Distro\Prerequisites folder are missing or no longer match the hash recorded when they were stored, or which was removed from the library or is not in it, or depends on one that was. Nothing was installed.

**What to do:**

- Open the Prerequisites screen: an item whose files do not match says so. Replace its files there, which records the new hash.
- An item removed from the library cannot be used again: leave it out of the image or job, or add it again on the Prerequisites screen, where it gets a new ID.
- Nothing but the Prerequisites screen should write into Distro\Prerequisites.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-SG` — Signing

### `AP-SG-005` — The publisher change cannot be bridged

Bridging a publisher change needs the catalog signed with the previous certificate. Its private key is no longer available, so continuity with already-deployed packages cannot be established.

**What to do:**

- If the old private key exists anywhere, import it and re-run.
- Otherwise the new package is a separate identity: deployed installs will not upgrade in place and need removing and reinstalling.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-006` — Adding certificate trust did not return

A write to a certificate store raised a consent dialog in a session with no interactive desktop, so nothing could answer it and the call never returned.

**Observed:** A CurrentUser\Root add raising a consent dialog in a non-interactive session, blocking until killed.

**What to do:**

- Use LocalMachine\Root from an elevated context rather than CurrentUser\Root, which prompts.
- This is development-only trust provisioning. A CA-issued certificate needs none of it.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-007` — The package's Publisher does not match the signing certificate

MSIX requires the manifest's Publisher to be character-for-character identical to the signing certificate's subject. Anything else is refused at signing, including a difference in spacing or attribute order.

**Observed:** signtool refusing the package with 0x8007000B, 'the app manifest publisher name must match the subject name of the signing certificate'.

**What to do:**

- The product rewrites the Publisher from the certificate subject before signing, so seeing this means the rewrite was skipped or the certificate changed afterwards.
- Compare the two exactly. 'CN=Contoso, O=Contoso' and 'CN=Contoso,O=Contoso' are different strings and only one of them will work.
- If the publisher genuinely changed, the new package is a different identity to Windows and existing installs will not upgrade in place. See AP-SG-005 on bridging.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-008` — The package could not be signed

SignTool refused the signature or could not complete it, and the cause was not the manifest publisher. The package is unsigned and has not left this machine.

**What to do:**

- For Azure Artifact Signing, confirm the account running the product is signed in (az login) and holds the Artifact Signing Certificate Profile Signer role on the profile.
- For a certificate in the Windows store, confirm it is still there, still has its private key, and is not on a hardware token waiting for a PIN nobody will type.
- If the timestamp server was unreachable, the file was left completely unsigned rather than partly signed, so retrying once the network is back is safe.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-SG-009` — The publisher has changed too many times to bridge

Each change of signing publisher adds one bridging artifact to the package, and Windows applies at most five. This change would need a sixth, so the package cannot keep the identity that already-deployed installs have.

**What to do:**

- Sign with a publisher already in the chain, which needs no new artifact.
- Otherwise the new package is a separate identity: deployed installs will not upgrade in place and need removing and reinstalling.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-010` — The tools that sign packages can be changed by somebody who is not an administrator

The application runs signtool, makecat and makeappx elevated from the Tools folder. They work on the package in its job folder, and the application signs the packages in the Packages folder. An account that is not an administrator can change one of these folders, or a folder above them. So the tool did not start, and the job, Retry signing or the signing test stopped.

**What to do:**

- Run host preparation (AutomatedPackaging.PrepareHost.exe) and fix "Working directory access" - or "Data folder access" on a host with no working directory. It closes the tree to Administrators, Hyper-V Administrators and SYSTEM and takes back what somebody else owns.
- The refusal names who and where. A link in the tree, or a folder above it that somebody else can change, is not fixed for you: remove the link or correct that folder by hand.
- Anything the fix took back from another account is named in its outcome. If you did not put it there, look at what it is before running a job.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-011` — The package changed after the job built it, so it was not signed

The job recorded the package's SHA-256 when it packed it. Before it signs, the application reads the package again and compares. The package was different, was gone, was a link or had a second name, or the job has no recorded hash. Somebody or something changed it in the job folder. It was not signed with your certificate.

**What to do:**

- Rebuild the job. A package that changed cannot be re-signed: nothing says what is in it now.
- Run host preparation and fix "Working directory access", so that only administrators can change the job folders.
- If you did not change the package, look at who could write the job folder before you rebuild.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-012` — AI agents do not sign on this host

An AI agent asked for a job through MCP. A job signs its package, and on this host agents do not sign. A package carries the identity of the certificate that signs it.

**What to do:**

- Build the job on the Build screen or with the command line.
- To let agents sign, go to Settings > AI agents (MCP). Select Ask each time or Allowed, then select the certificates.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-013` — Nobody confirmed that the agent's job can sign

On this host, the MCP client asks before an agent's job signs. The question was declined, cancelled, or the client cannot ask questions. Nothing was signed.

**What to do:**

- Start the job again and accept the question in your MCP client.
- Use an MCP client that can ask questions, or build the job on the Build screen.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-VF` — Verification

### `AP-VF-001` — The finished package would not install

The smoke test ran Add-AppxPackage against the package this job produced and Windows refused it. The package is not usable, and the job fails here rather than at a customer.

**Observed:** Add-AppxPackage failing on a package the conversion reported as successful.

**What to do:**

- 0x80073CF3 means a declared framework dependency is not present. That is the spurious Windows App SDK dependency MPT injects, and it should have been stripped; see AP-PK-006.
- 0x800B0109 means the signing certificate is not trusted on this machine. A CA-issued certificate needs no trust provisioning; a self-signed one does.
- 0x80073D02 means a package with the same identity is already installed and running.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-VF-002` — The packaged application would not start

The package installed cleanly and the application did not launch. The package deploys and does nothing, which is the failure a smoke test exists to catch.

**What to do:**

- Check the manifest's entry point actually exists in the payload. A shortcut pointing at something the installer did not place produces exactly this.
- An application that needs a PSF fixup to find its own files often fails here first.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-VF-003` — The packaged application started and closed immediately

The application launched and was gone before the settle period ended. It crashed on startup rather than failing to start, which usually means it could not find something it expected.

**What to do:**

- Check whether the application writes to its own install directory on first run. That needs the FileRedirectionFixup, and without it the application dies here.
- Check the guest's Application event log for the crash, which names the missing assembly or file far more usefully than this does.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-VF-004` — The signing certificate is not trusted on the target

The package is correctly built and correctly signed, and the machine installing it does not trust the certificate that signed it. Nothing is wrong with the package.

**Observed:** Add-AppxPackage failing 0x800B0109 on a package that installs correctly on a machine where the issuing certificate is present.

**What to do:**

- A certificate from a public CA needs no trust provisioning at all; that is the practical difference between a real certificate and a test one.
- For an internal CA, the issuing certificate has to be in Trusted Root or Trusted People on every target machine, which is normally a Group Policy or Intune deployment.
- For a self-signed certificate, every target needs that specific certificate. That does not scale and is a development convenience rather than a deployment approach.
- Trust provisioning belongs to the deployment channel, not to this product. A package that installs only because the packaging tool trusted something is not a package that will install anywhere else.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-LC` — Licence

### `AP-LC-001` — The licence file is not valid

Signature verification failed. A forged or malformed licence is not a soft condition, so the product refuses to run rather than degrading.

**What to do:**

- Re-download the licence file; the commonest cause is a file damaged in transit or edited by hand.
- If it still fails, contact support with the licence identifier.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-LC-002` — The licence has expired and is in its grace period

Builds still run for 30 days past expiry, with a persistent banner. This is a warning, not a failure.

**What to do:**

- Renew the licence before the grace period ends.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-LC-003` — The licence has expired

The 30-day grace period is over, so new builds are refused. Job history, logs, output and the diagnostics bundle stay fully accessible: nobody is locked out of their own data.

**What to do:**

- Renew the licence to resume building.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-LC-004` — The licence expires soon

Shown from 60 days before expiry. Purely a warning; nothing is restricted yet.

**What to do:**

- Arrange renewal.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-LC-005` — The system clock has moved backwards

The clock is significantly earlier than the latest date previously recorded. Small backward movements are tolerated for timezone changes, VM restores and genuine drift; a large jump is refused.

**What to do:**

- Set the system clock correctly.
- If the machine was restored from an old backup or image, correcting the clock resolves this.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-LC-006` — The starter allowance is used

With no licence installed, this installation may build one image and five packages, counted over its lifetime: deleting an image or a package does not free its place. The allowance is used, so new builds are refused. Job history, logs, output and the images and packages already made stay fully available, and the image already built can still be updated and rebuilt.

**What to do:**

- Install a licence under Settings > Licence to build more.
- A community licence is free: ask for one.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-LC-007` — The licence does not include MCP

The host service accepts an MCP client only with a licence that includes the mcp feature. The starter allowance and a community licence do not include it.

**What to do:**

- Install a Basic licence that includes MCP under Settings > Licence.
- Ask your supplier for a new licence file if your Basic licence does not include MCP.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.
